name: PC (Polycarbonate)
chemical_makeup: Bisphenol-A polycarbonate — an amorphous engineering thermoplastic. Catalog blends such as PC-ABS and PC-PBT share this base chemistry with toughening or flow modifiers
summary: The high-temperature structural workhorse of desktop FDM: the best heat resistance, stiffness and sustained-load performance of the common materials, with impact toughness to match. The price is process difficulty — 250-310 °C nozzle temperatures, an enclosure that is effectively mandatory, and hygroscopy on par with nylon.

printing.notes: Sources cluster into two bands: Polymaker PolyMax PC runs cooler at 250-270 °C, while Prusa (275 °C ±10) and Simplify3D (260-310 °C) push higher. Start at 275 °C and tune for layer bonding. Keep part cooling near zero — excessive cooling is the main cause of layer separation in PC. Drop to 20-40 mm/s for large or warp-prone geometry. An enclosure is near-required and 45-70 °C ambient is the target; an actively heated chamber is strongly beneficial for medium and large parts but is not the hard prerequisite it is for PEEK-class polymers, so heated_chamber_required is recorded as false. Unfilled PC prints fine on stock brass or steel nozzles; CF/GF PC variants need a hardened nozzle.

methods: print directly from a heated dryer
drying.dryness_validation: Clear, glossy extrudate rather than hazy, matte or bubbly; no popping or hissing at the nozzle; consistent extrusion width; the part does not snap brittly on a test coupon
drying.notes: Prusa describes PC as 'extremely hygroscopic'. Polymaker specifies 75 °C for 6 h on PolyMax PC; saturated spools benefit from longer. Prusament PC Blend is noted to absorb moisture much less than standard polycarbonates, so drying rigour is partly brand-dependent.

storage.recommendations: Airtight container with desiccant, with minimal ambient exposure between prints; print from a drybox or heated dryer for long jobs. Standard PC is at the extreme end of hygroscopy, while some PC blends are merely high.

price.notes: 2025-2026 pricing for standard unfilled PC: Polymaker PolyMax PC $38.99/0.75 kg (~$52/kg) or $144.99/3 kg (~$48/kg); Bambu and other mainstream brands generally $30-45/kg. Precise low end unverified.

recommended: functional prototypes needing heat plus impact resistance
optically clear lens and light-guide parts on clear grades
not_recommended: food-contact items (standard grades are not food-safe)
quick low-effort prints (drying plus enclosure overhead)
fine-detail miniatures (high temperatures worsen stringing and detail)
long-term outdoor UV exposure without coating or stabiliser

properties.notes: Density 1.19-1.20 g/cm³. Shrinkage is numerically low-moderate yet PC still warps badly, because the driver is thermal stress from the high processing temperature rather than crystallisation. Tg is recorded at 145 °C to reflect general BPA-PC literature (~150 °C); Polymaker's PolyMax PC measured 113 °C by DSC, which likely reflects a modified grade. HDT@0.45 MPa: PolyMax PC 114 °C (HDT@1.8 MPa 99 °C), general literature to 140 °C. Tensile: PolyMax PC 53.4 MPa XY and 41.4 MPa Z, partmfg 52 MPa, 3dprinterly up to 65 MPa.

compatibility.notes: PC has the best cross-material affinity of the engineering trio: it is chemically related to ABS (PC-ABS blends are a commercial product) and interfaces can partially fuse, with ASA a weaker second. It does not weld reliably to pla, petg, pa, pp, pctg, pvb, pet, tpu or tpe. Prusa explicitly notes BVOH and HIPS as compatible supports including via MMU2/3; PVA is unsuitable because it degrades well below PC's print temperature. PC is not used as a support for other polymers — its melt temperature is too high and it bonds too aggressively.

plate_recommendations.notes: Textured/satin PEI at ~90-115 °C bed is the recommended surface. Prusa explicitly warns against smooth PEI, where PC's adhesion is strong enough to tear the sheet. Use a glue stick as a SEPARATOR/release layer to protect the plate, matching the pattern for PETG and TPU rather than nylon's promoter role.

primary_emissions: unspecified VOCs (no single dominant marker compound identified in the sources reviewed)
emissions.notes: Prusa describes a moderate odour. PC's VOC profile is less characterised in the literature than nylon's caprolactam or ABS's styrene, so no marker compound is named here. UFP emission is moderate and brand/temperature dependent, sitting between the PLA and ABS extremes in the built-envi summary of ACS EST studies. Because PC is printed hot and enclosed, extended sessions should be vented or filtered rather than run in an occupied room.

safety_notes: Standard grades are bisphenol-A based, which is a further reason to keep them out of food- and drink-contact uses regardless of print-surface hygiene. The 250-310 °C hotend and 90-120 °C bed are burn hazards, and a hot enclosure concentrates off-gassing — vent before opening the door.
additional_notes: PC's weakness is process, not material: dry, hot and enclosed it delivers the strongest, most heat-tolerant parts in this catalog, but under-dried or under-enclosed it delaminates and prints worse than ABS. PC blends (PC-ABS, PC-PBT, Prusament PC Blend) trade some heat resistance for markedly easier printing and lower moisture uptake and are the pragmatic choice for most users.

provenance.conflicts: Glass transition is the main disagreement: Polymaker measured 113 °C by DSC on PolyMax PC while Simplify3D and general PC literature cite ~150 °C — the gap most likely reflects different grades and measurement conditions; 145 °C is recorded for generic BPA-PC and the Polymaker figure is preserved in properties.notes. Nozzle temperature splits similarly: Polymaker 250-270 °C vs Simplify3D 260-310 °C. Tensile strength spans 41-72 MPa across sources and is strongly anisotropic (PolyMax XY 53.4 vs Z 41.4 MPa). Hygroscopy is brand-dependent — Prusa calls standard PC extremely hygroscopic while noting Prusament PC Blend absorbs far less. Water tolerance is scored 5 as a compromise: PC as a filament behaves like nylon, but a finished PC part is far less water-permeable than a nylon one. The low end of the price range is unverified.
